newsitem.title: USA: Rep Roukema has no specific concerns on BT merger.
newsitem.headline: Rep Roukema has no specific concerns on BT merger.

text.p: A top U.S. lawmaker called Monday for Congressional hearings on Bankers Trust Corp of New York's $1.7 billion acquisition of Alex. Brown Inc, saying she was interested in the implications of the merger on the debate over modernization of banking laws.

Rep. Marge Roukema, chairwoman of the House Banking Committee's Financial Institutions subcommittee, told Reuters in a telephone interview Monday that she was not challenging the Bankers Trust merger.
"I don't have specific reason to be worried about this particular merger," the New Jersey Republican said.
"I want to relate it to the larger question, the issues as they relate to financial modernization," Roukema said.

"I have stressed for more than a year that we in Congress should not be abdicating our responsibility," she added. "We should move forward with this and not leave it to the regulators on an ad hoc basis."

The Glass Steagall Act of 1933 generally prohibits banks from acquiring securities firms. But since 1987, Federal Reserve has interpreted Section 20 of the Act to allow banks to have limited securities subsidiaries.

Congress has debated scrapping the Act for years. Last year, after proposals to overhaul banking laws failed, the Fed more than doubled its limit on the amount of revenue a bank could earn from securities activity.
Roukema said all the participants in the debate ought to support a legislative overhaul of banking laws.

"I think that there is no reason to further move away from the table," she said. "This is the time to put everybody together. They're all at the table now in one form or another and the time is right."
Roukema has introduced a proposal backed by a coalition of financial sector trade groups that would scrap Glass Steagall and allow banks to combine with insurance companies and securities firms.
The bill would also allow a financial services company to conduct up to 25 percent of its business activity in nonfinancial, commercial businesses.
House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach has introduced a bill that would also scrap Glass Steagall but would maintain strict limits on combinations of financial and nonfinancial companies.
Leach agreed that the Bankers Trust acquisition demonstrated the need for legislative reform.
"This proposed merger simply underscores the need for timely Congressional action on bank modernization legislation," the Iowa Republican said Monday in a statement.

"While the merger of this relatively large bank with a regional securities firm fits the constraints of current Federal Reserve guidelines, other prospective changes on Wall Street require that the market place be rationalized in an orderly fashion for all financial services market participants," she added.
The ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee, Texas Rep Henry Gonzalez, said the safety and soundness of the banking system could be jeopardized by ad hoc mergers.

"As it is today, it is only a matter of luck that restructuring deals like this will truly serve the best interests of the market and the people who depend on it," Gonzalez said in a statement. "Congress can't afford to do nothing and hope that everything will be all right."
